Before that: IBM, and trading.  
  
What is OpenBot   
OpenBot is a free, open-source alternative to Grok Bot - a team of AI agents that runs locally on your own computer instead of cloud. Plug in the ChatGPT, Claude, Grok or OpenCode subscription you already have, no extra bill.   
It also has a multiplayer mode, so your whole team can share a project and talk to the same agents together, live.  
  
The problem   
Grok Bot showed where AI is headed - agents that work for you. But it runs on a Linux server in the cloud: plenty of apps just don't work there, websites often flag and block that kind of server traffic outright, it costs $200-300/month on top of what you already pay, and there's no way for a team to actually work with the same agents together.

results.title: 8 Best Open Source Grok Bot Alternatives in 2026
results.content:
Pricing and access

No standalone plan, no free tier. Eligible: SuperGrok Plus/Heavy, Cursor Pro+ ($60), Ultra ($200), Teams ($40/user). Weekly usage included; on-demand extra.

All eight are free and open source. Variable costs: model API calls, a VPS or local Docker host, optional paid sandboxes (E2B, Daytona, Box), optional managed services (Nous Portal, openhuman subscription), and ElevenLabs for voice in openmausbot.

Model choice

Grok Bot runs on xAI's own models, and xAI documents no way to substitute another.

Six of eight offer native model choice; buzz and paperclip delegate model selection to their connected agents. rakazo uses any provider via Pi or OpenRouter, openbot accepts any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and openclaw works with any hosted or local provider. [...] rakazo, openmausbot, openhuman, and openbot: browser, terminal, and file access. hermes-agent: cloud browser via Nous Portal. paperclip orchestrates but does not itself provide compute. buzz is a workspace surface. openclaw has a browser tool on a local profile, enabled per agent.

Hosting and source

Closed source. Cloud-only on xAI/Cursor infrastructure. No self-hosting option and no documented export path for skills or routines you build.

All eight are open source. Seven self-host via Docker or a native installer. Licenses range from MIT and Apache-2.0 to GPL-3.0 (openhuman). None require xAI infrastructure and all expose their full source for audit.

Pricing and access [...] What does Grok Bot cost and is there a free tier?

No free tier, no standalone plan. Eligible plans are SuperGrok Plus and Heavy, Cursor Pro+ ($60/mo), Cursor Ultra ($200/mo), and Cursor Teams ($40/user/mo); Cursor's pricing page also marks Grok Bot on its $20 Pro plan, so check there for the latest. xAI's docs show the subscription includes weekly Grok Bot usage; on-demand usage bills by model and token cost on top. All eight alternatives are free and open source. Recurring costs depend on how you run them: model API calls, a VPS or Docker host, and optionally paid sandboxes, managed services, or voice APIs.
